report.title: A Sinclair Henderson Trust
report.quote: Fund award sizes. Average: Premium information. Annually awarded: Premium information. Notes on award amounts: Premium information.
report.note: The trust has no site of its own — applications go to Thorntons solicitors by email — so funding.scot is the only page there is. It has an award-sizes section and every figure in it is behind SCVO membership. A listing with the number paywalled is the one case where following the brief's listing rule leaves nothing at all.

report.title: Accelerate
report.quote: The programme offers up to 6 days of flexible 1:1 support, tailored to each organisation's needs.
report.note: Free consultancy days rather than money. The only "up to" on the page counts days.

report.title: Accelerated Growth Programme — Business Wales
report.quote: Accelerating success: How the Accelerated Growth Programme helped tech recruitment specialist Accelero break through £1m and scale strategically
report.note: Advisory support, not a grant. Every pound on the page is a case-study outcome — a company reaching £1m turnover, another raising £700,000 — and none is anything a participant receives.

report.title: Albert Gubay Charitable Foundation Grants
report.quote: Since 2016, the Albert Gubay Charitable Foundation has awarded over £100 million to registered charities in England, the Isle of Man, Republic of Ireland, and Wales.
report.note: Cumulative giving since 2016, alongside a "£90 Million Given In Grants" banner and the £700 million Albert Gubay's businesses were worth. No per-grant figure anywhere.

report.title: Albert Hunt Trust
report.quote: We are committed to providing unrestricted core funding to help with your general running costs for example towards your bills or rent and towards your overall salary bill.
report.note: A full FAQ covering eligibility, timing, reapplication and the trust's spend-down to 2029, with no figure of any kind. The quote is the closest it comes to describing what a grant covers.

report.title: Arnold Clark Community Fund
report.quote: The Arnold Clark Community Fund welcomes applications from registered charities and community groups located within 50 miles of an Arnold Clark branch.
report.note: The fund page carries no pound sign at all — the quote is eligibility rather than money, because there is no money sentence to quote. Three funding categories are named without amounts.

report.title: Backstage Trust performing arts grants
report.quote: There is no specified minimum or maximum amount you can apply for.
report.note: The row the brief names. Funding for All prints "Up to: £500000" in its own header field and the trust's own words on the same page are the quote above. The trust does not operate a website, so there is no funder page to go to. Nothing written.

report.title: Barbara Ward Children's Foundation
report.quote: Since then the Trustees have reviewed more than 7600 grant requests and authorised grants of over £12 million to more than 465 organisations.
report.note: Cumulative since 2001. £12 million over 465 organisations averages around £26,000, but an average of a lifetime total is not a figure the foundation states and is not written.

report.title: Barrow Cadbury Trust Grants
report.quote: If, following submission of your enquiry form, you are invited to make a full application, the assessment and decision process at the application form stage may take up to four months.
report.note: The applying-for-funding page has no figure. The only "up to" on it counts months.

report.title: BCG UK Social Enterprise Award
report.quote: Every organisation that makes it to the semi-final will receive coaching from BCG employees in the lead-up to our pitching events.
report.note: The award is a consulting engagement rather than cash. The £500k on the page is a turnover floor for applicants, which belongs in min_org_income and not here.

report.title: Bernard Sunley Foundation — Capital Grants
report.quote: Project costs between £10,000 and £5 million.
report.note: See the header note. The quote is the size of PROJECT the foundation considers, not the size of grant, and is deliberately not written to the columns. The three grant bands (large £25,000 and above, medium up to £20,000, small £5,000 and under) exist only inside a JavaScript data attribute and never as page text, so they cannot carry a citation the checker could match. Worth someone reading the site in a browser and setting these by hand.

report.title: Bernard Sunley Foundation — Social Welfare Grants
report.quote: Project costs between £10,000 and £5 million.
report.note: Second row on the same foundation and the same problem. apply_url here is the social-welfare page, which renders its grant table in JavaScript and reads as a list of categories with nothing under them.

report.title: BlueSpark Foundation
report.quote: We are a registered charity providing grants for educational, cultural, sporting and other projects.
report.note: A 178KB site describing the kinds of project it funds, with no pound sign anywhere on the home page and no separate how-much page.

report.title: British Record Industry Trust (Brit Trust)
report.quote: The BRIT Trust Grant application window for 2026 is now closed. Applications for 2027 will open towards the end of this year.
report.note: An 11KB page that says when the round runs and nothing about how much.

report.title: Cadent Foundation — Community Grants
report.quote: This is made possible each year by Cadent who help to fund the Cadent Foundation by committing £3 million annually of post-tax profits.
report.note: Two pots on one page, £3 million a year into the foundation and a £1m Warm Fund inside it, and no per-grant figure. Grants are administered by Charities Trust, which may hold the figure.

report.title: CAF Venturesome Impact Fund
report.quote: Since 2002 we have lent more than £65 million to over 500 charities, social enterprises and community groups.
report.note: Cumulative lending since 2002. An investment row, so a ticket range would be the figure to hold, and the page states none.

report.title: Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation UK Branch — Grants
report.quote: The UK Branch aims to strengthen arts and civil society ecosystems by supporting transnational exchange, reciprocal capacity development and knowledge sharing between Portugal and the UK.
report.note: No pound sign on the page. Same row reported as not_stated in the timing job for the same reason: the grant-making page describes what the branch funds and nothing about how much or when.

report.title: Camden Climate Fund
report.quote: Just a moment...
report.note: HTTP 403 behind a Cloudflare interstitial, as in the timing job.

report.title: Canva for Nonprofits
report.quote: Client Challenge. A required part of this site couldn't load.
report.note: A bot wall that returns HTTP 200 with a 3KB challenge page. Distinct from a 403 and easy to mistake for a thin page.

report.title: Cash for Kids - Cost of Living Grants
report.quote: Please check the specific Eligibility Criteria for the grant you are applying for.
report.note: Grants are run by Local Executive Boards area by area, each with its own criteria and its own money, and the national page states no figure for any of them.

report.title: Cash for Kids - General Grant
report.quote: Please check the specific Eligibility Criteria for the grant you are applying for.
report.note: Second Cash for Kids row pointing at the identical URL as the Cost of Living row above. Worth checking whether these are two funds or one row duplicated.

report.title: CAST — Free Digital and AI Support for Charities
report.quote: What you talk about will be entirely up to you and your match: it could be a challenge you need help with, advice you'd like to share, or just a general chat about digital, data or design.
report.note: Peer matching and programmes rather than money.

report.title: Chalk Cliff Trust — Grants for East Sussex
report.quote: The Chalk Cliff Trust is a foundation set up to provide grants and donations to charities, action groups and benevolent organisations predominantly in the East Sussex area.
report.note: A 141KB site with a single sentence about what it does and no figure anywhere.

report.title: Champions for Children — Match Fundraising Programme
report.quote: We use the Big Give's pledge model of funding for our two match-funding programmes. Our model enhances donations made by the public on the Big Give platform, helping charities to raise even more funds.
report.note: Match funding, which the brief excludes from the columns by name: what a charity receives depends on what it raises. The £5.8 million on the page is the 2024 campaign total across almost 170,000 children, and the £500,000 is an income ceiling for the entry-level strand. The amount columns are also admin-pinned here, so nothing would have been written in any case.

report.title: Charity Digital Skills Programme
report.quote: Join us for a one-hour session to master AI prompts. For just £20, you'll supercharge your productivity.
report.note: The only pounds on the page are a course fee the charity pays, and the only "up to" counts free Adobe Express licences. Money flowing the wrong way, like Clore below.

report.title: Charterpath Pro Bono Accountancy for Charities
report.quote: For non-profits
report.note: A 998KB Wix page whose readable text is navigation. Pro bono accountancy rather than money, and no pound sign in what renders.

report.title: Church and Communities Programme
report.quote: In 2024-25 our Church & Communities programme awarded £3.4 million over 70 grants to 57* organisations in Greater London, Lincolnshire, Norfolk and the North East of England.
report.note: A programme total. It divides to roughly £49,000 a grant, which is exactly the sort of arithmetic the brief rules out: the foundation states no per-applicant figure and a derived average would be a number nobody published.

report.title: Civitates — Pooled Fund for European Democracy
report.quote: Since then, our pooled fund has supported more than 90 organisations to defend the key pillars of democracy in 20+ European countries with a total of €20 million, and growing.
report.note: A cumulative total, and in euros. Nothing per applicant.

report.title: Clore Social Leadership Programme
report.quote: £1,995 Early Bird
report.note: See the header note. The three figures on this page (£1,995, £2,395 and £3,550 Early Bird) are course fees the participant pays, sitting in exactly the place an amount scraper would look for an award. Nothing is given.

report.title: Commissioned Rehabilitative Services General Grant Scheme
report.quote: Each of these regions has access to a budget per financial year that can be used to commission rehabilitative services.
report.note: A Find a grant listing with Summary, Eligibility, Objectives, Dates and How to apply sections and no value field filled in. The budget referred to is a probation region's, not an award.

report.title: Community Energy GO!
report.quote: We're a key player in this £5m initiative, working with communities to speed up Bristol and the West of England's transition to net zero.
report.note: The £5m belongs to a different CSE initiative on the same page, not to Community Energy GO, which is free advisory support with no grant attached.

report.title: Community Grants (The Old Enfield Charitable Trust)
report.quote: In a typical year The Old Enfield Charitable Trust administers around £250K in discretionary grants to families, individuals and community groups.
report.note: An annual total spread across three kinds of recipient, so it will not even divide meaningfully. Amount columns are admin-pinned on this row.

report.title: Community Grants (Hampton Fund)
report.quote: Our Trustees meet four times a year – in March, June, September and December - to assess applications and approve grants.
report.note: No pound sign on the page. The same row was reported in the timing job because its deadlines are "available on request"; the amounts are not published either. Amount columns admin-pinned.

report.title: Continuo Foundation Project Grants
report.quote: From the outset, Continuo Foundation has been offering a minimum of £200,000 per year in project grants across two rounds.
report.note: A floor on the fund's annual giving, not a floor on an award. The nearest trap in the batch: "a minimum of £200,000" reads like amount_min and is the opposite of one.

report.title: Cornwall Community Foundation — Community Grants
report.quote: Grant value: Organisations may apply for up to £3,000
report.note: A rich index: at least seven named funds each printing its own "Grant value" line, ranging from £250 to £5,000, plus one offering mentoring with a grant of up to £1,000. Every figure on the page belongs to a specific fund and none to this funder-level row.
